propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui hodierna die beatum Dionysium, Martyrem tuum atque Pontificem,
virtute constantiae in passione roborasti, quique illi, ad praedicandum
gentibus gloriam tuam, Rusticum et Eleutherium sociare dignatus es: tribue
nobis, quaesumus; eorum imitatione, pro amore tuo prospera mundi despicere,
et nulla ejus adversa formidare. Per Dominum.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

translations.source_label: The New Roman Missal in Latin and English, revised edition, by F. X. Lasance and Francis Augustine Walsh (New York: Benziger Brothers, 1945), ca. 1955-56 printing (Internet Archive delivery locator fr-lasance-missal-1937; locator mislabelled)
translations.text: O God, Who on this day didst strengthen blessed Dionysius, Thy martyr, with the virtue of fortitude in his suffering, and didst vouchsafe to join with him Rusticus and Eleutherius to preach Thy glory to the nations, grant us, we beseech Thee, to imitate them in contemning the prosperity of the world for the sake of Thy love, and to fear none of its adversity. Through our Lord.

Martyribus tuis Dionysio, Rustico et Eleutherio, ad redemptionis aeternae

tecum vivit et regnat.
